\NormalTok{list\_of\_sectors }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Hunting"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"Utilities"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"Construction"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"Manufacturing"}\NormalTok{,}
\StringTok{"Wholesale Trade"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"Retail Trade"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"Transportation and Warehousing"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"Information"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{"Finance and Insurance"}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# For loop that includes instructions that refer to a variable that doesn\textquotesingle{}t exist.}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ (x }\ControlFlowTok{in}\NormalTok{ list\_of\_sectors) \{}
  \FunctionTok{print}\NormalTok{(sector\_name)}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
## Error in print(sector_name): object 'sector_name' not found
\end{verbatim}

We can also write for loops to iterate over a range of numbers, instead of a list of characters. The syntax is a little different.

The code below says: ``for each number in a range of numbers from 1 to 10, print the number.''

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# For loop that includes instructions that refer to a variable that doesn\textquotesingle{}t exist.}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ (number }\ControlFlowTok{in} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{:}\DecValTok{10}\NormalTok{) \{}
  \FunctionTok{print}\NormalTok{(number)}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
## [1] 1
## [1] 2
## [1] 3
## [1] 4
## [1] 5
## [1] 6
## [1] 7
## [1] 8
## [1] 9
## [1] 10
\end{verbatim}

Here's a minor variation on that approach that we'll make use of below.

Instead of giving the for loop an explicit number range, like 1:10, we can tell it to use 1 to ``the number of rows in a dataframe'' as our list of things to loop through.

Remember the naics\_industry dataframe we loaded first? It has 20 rows.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{naics\_industry}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
## # A tibble: 20 x 2
##    sector description                                                           
##    <chr>  <chr>                                                                 
##  1 11     Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Hunting                            
##  2 21     Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction                         
##  3 22     Utilities                                                             
##  4 23     Construction                                                          
##  5 31-33  Manufacturing                                                         
##  6 42     Wholesale Trade                                                       
##  7 44-45  Retail Trade                                                          
##  8 48-49  Transportation and Warehousing                                        
##  9 51     Information                                                           
## 10 52     Finance and Insurance                                                 
## 11 53     Real Estate and Rental and Leasing                                    
## 12 54     Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services                      
## 13 55     Management of Companies and Enterprises                               
## 14 56     Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Servi~
## 15 61     Educational Services                                                  
## 16 62     Health Care and Social Assistance                                     
## 17 71     Arts, Entertainment, and Recreation                                   
## 18 72     Accommodation and Food Services                                       
## 19 81     Other Services (except Public Administration)                         
## 20 92     Public Administration
\end{verbatim}

We can use that information in our for loop by using the nrow() function, which calculates the number of rows in a dataframe. Here's a quick demonstration of how that works.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\FunctionTok{nrow}\NormalTok{(naics\_industry)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
## [1] 20
\end{verbatim}

To put it all together, the code below says ``make a list of numbers that starts at 1 and ends at the number of rows in the naics\_industry dataframe (which is 20), then print out each of these numbers.''

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# For loop that includes instructions that refer to a variable that doesn\textquotesingle{}t exist.}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{ (row\_number }\ControlFlowTok{in} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{:}\FunctionTok{nrow}\NormalTok{(naics\_industry)) \{}
  \FunctionTok{print}\NormalTok{(row\_number)}
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
## [1] 1
## [1] 2
## [1] 3
## [1] 4
## [1] 5
## [1] 6
## [1] 7
## [1] 8
## [1] 9
## [1] 10
## [1] 11
## [1] 12
## [1] 13
## [1] 14
## [1] 15
## [1] 16
## [1] 17
## [1] 18
## [1] 19
## [1] 20
\end{verbatim}

These were basic examples of how ``for loops'' work. Next, we'll learn to apply ``for loops'' to efficentily extract information from multiple web pages.

\hypertarget{looping-and-rvest}{%
\section{Looping and rvest}\label{looping-and-rvest}}

First, let's look at the codeblock we wrote earlier to extract the number of employees in the mining sector.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Define url of the page we want to get}
\NormalTok{url }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \StringTok{"https://www.bls.gov/iag/tgs/iag21.htm"}

\CommentTok{\# Get employment html page and select only the table with employment information, then transform it from html to a table.}
\NormalTok{employment\_info }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ url }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{read\_html}\NormalTok{() }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{html\_element}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{xpath =} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}//*[@id="iag21emp1"]\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{html\_table}\NormalTok{() }

\CommentTok{\# Keep only second row with seasonally adjusted, bind back to each\_row\_df}
\NormalTok{employment\_info }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ employment\_info }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{clean\_names}\NormalTok{() }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{slice}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{select}\NormalTok{(data\_series, jul\_2021)}

\CommentTok{\# Display it so we can see what it looks like}
\NormalTok{employment\_info}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
## # A tibble: 1 x 2
##   data_series                                      jul_2021
##   <chr>                                            <chr>   
## 1 Employment, all employees  (seasonally adjusted) 592.5
\end{verbatim}

This contains all the steps we needed to extract the information from one sector page. We're now going to modify this function so we can use it to extract information from each sector page, writing code that keeps us from repeating ourselves too much.\\
First, we need to build a list of URLs to loop through in a ``for loop.'' We can do that using the dataframe we made in the last chapter.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Define url of page we want to scrape}

\NormalTok{naics\_url }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \StringTok{"https://www.bls.gov/ces/naics/"}

\CommentTok{\# Read in all html from table, store all tables on page as nested list of dataframes.}
\NormalTok{naics\_industry  }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ naics\_url }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{read\_html}\NormalTok{() }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{html\_table}\NormalTok{()}

\CommentTok{\# Just keep the second dataframe in our list, standardize column headers, remove last row}

\NormalTok{naics\_industry }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ naics\_industry[[}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{]] }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{clean\_names}\NormalTok{() }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{slice}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\DecValTok{21}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# show the dataframe}
\NormalTok{naics\_industry}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
## # A tibble: 20 x 2
##    sector description                                                           
##    <chr>  <chr>                                                                 
##  1 11     Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Hunting                            
##  2 21     Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction                         
##  3 22     Utilities                                                             
##  4 23     Construction                                                          
##  5 31-33  Manufacturing                                                         
##  6 42     Wholesale Trade                                                       
##  7 44-45  Retail Trade                                                          
##  8 48-49  Transportation and Warehousing                                        
##  9 51     Information                                                           
## 10 52     Finance and Insurance                                                 
## 11 53     Real Estate and Rental and Leasing                                    
## 12 54     Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services                      
## 13 55     Management of Companies and Enterprises                               
## 14 56     Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Servi~
## 15 61     Educational Services                                                  
## 16 62     Health Care and Social Assistance                                     
## 17 71     Arts, Entertainment, and Recreation                                   
## 18 72     Accommodation and Food Services                                       
## 19 81     Other Services (except Public Administration)                         
## 20 92     Public Administration
\end{verbatim}

This gives us the sector code and name for each industry.

Now let's have a look at the URLs for a few of the pages we want to grab data from.

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction: \url{https://www.bls.gov/iag/tgs/iag21.htm}.
\item
  Utilities: \url{https://www.bls.gov/iag/tgs/iag22.htm}.
\item
  Construction: \url{https://www.bls.gov/iag/tgs/iag23.htm}
\end{itemize}

Notice a pattern?

They all start with ``\url{https://www.bls.gov/iag/tgs/iag}''. The next bit of information is different for each one; with the two-digit sector code for each sector. The remainder is identical in all three links, ``.htm''.

Because they're all the same, we can use the information in the dataframe we just loaded to make all the URLs we need.

We're going to use mutate() and paste0() to concatenate (mash together) the things that stay constant in every url (the beginning and end) with the things that are different (the sector number, stored in the column called sector).

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Make a column with URL for each sector. }
\NormalTok{naics\_industry }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ naics\_industry }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{sector\_url =} \FunctionTok{paste0}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"https://www.bls.gov/iag/tgs/iag"}\NormalTok{,sector,}\StringTok{".htm"}\NormalTok{))}

\CommentTok{\# Display it}
\NormalTok{naics\_industry}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

While we're at it, we're going to use the same method to programatically build the ``xpath'' for the table on each sector page.

Recall that when we wrote our function that got information from just the mining page, the xpath targeted an element with an ID of ``iag21emp1''. Why 21? That's the sector code for mining.

If we look for that exact element ID on other sector pages, we won't find it! That's because it's different for each page.

On the Utilities page (sector code 22), the ID for the table we want is ``iag22emp1''. On the Construction page (sector code 23), it's ``iag23emp1''. We can also build this programatically, because it follows a predictable pattern.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Make a column with URL and xpath ID for each sector}
\NormalTok{naics\_industry }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ naics\_industry }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{sector\_url =} \FunctionTok{paste0}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"https://www.bls.gov/iag/tgs/iag"}\NormalTok{,sector,}\StringTok{".htm"}\NormalTok{)) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{sector\_xpath\_id =}\FunctionTok{paste0}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"iag"}\NormalTok{,sector,}\StringTok{"emp1"}\NormalTok{))}

\CommentTok{\# Display it}
\NormalTok{naics\_industry}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

Lastly, we're going to use filter to remove the ``Public Administration'' sector, because there's no page for it. We'll have to get that information some other way.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Make a column with URL and xpath ID for each sector, remove the Public Administration sector}
\NormalTok{naics\_industry }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ naics\_industry }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{sector\_url =} \FunctionTok{paste0}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"https://www.bls.gov/iag/tgs/iag"}\NormalTok{,sector,}\StringTok{".htm"}\NormalTok{)) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{sector\_xpath\_id =}\FunctionTok{paste0}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"iag"}\NormalTok{,sector,}\StringTok{"emp1"}\NormalTok{)) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{filter}\NormalTok{(description }\SpecialCharTok{!=} \StringTok{"Public Administration"}\NormalTok{)}
\CommentTok{\# Display it}
\NormalTok{naics\_industry}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

We're left with a dataframe of 19 rows and 4 columns. It now contains everything we need.

Next, we'll construct a ``for loop'' to extract the info we need from each page. We're going to build it up step-by-step, beginning with the the basic elements of our ``for loop''.

The codeblock below says: ``Make a list with the row numbers from 1 to the number of rows in our naics\_industry dataframe (which is 19). Then, for each element of that list (1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and so on up to 19), use slice() to keep only the one row that matches that number and save this newly created dataframe as each\_row\_df. Print out the dataframe. Then go to the next element on the list and do the same thing. Keep doing that until we hit number 19, then stop.''

We get 19 dataframes, each with one row, one for each sector.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# For loop, iterating over each row in our naics industry dataframe}

\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{(row\_number }\ControlFlowTok{in} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{:}\FunctionTok{nrow}\NormalTok{(naics\_industry)) \{}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Keep only the row for a given row number, get rid of every other row}
\NormalTok{    each\_row\_df }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ naics\_industry }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{slice}\NormalTok{(row\_number) }
    
    \CommentTok{\# To help us see what\textquotesingle{}s happening as we build this, we\textquotesingle{}re going to print the thing we\textquotesingle{}re creating.  }
    \FunctionTok{print}\NormalTok{(each\_row\_df)}
      
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

We're almost to the part where we can go out and fetch the html we need. Before we do that, let's store as part of our loop an object called ``url'', which contains the URL of the page for each sector.

The syntax with the dollar sign is a little funky, but ``each\_row\_df\$sector\_url'' says ``from the each\_row\_df dataframe, grab the information in the sector\_url column.'' Because the column has only one row, there's one value.

We're going to do something simliar with the xpath for our employment table by using the information in the sector\_xpath\_id column.

That code also looks a little unwieldly. Recall that the xpath for the mining industry was \texttt{\textquotesingle{}//*{[}@id="iag22emp1"{]}\textquotesingle{}}.

In the code below, we're building the xpath dynamically by pasting together the parts that stay the same for each xpath -- \texttt{\textquotesingle{}//*{[}@id="\textquotesingle{}} and \texttt{\textquotesingle{}"{]}\textquotesingle{}} -- and the parts that change for each sector, pulled from the xpath\_sector\_id column.

To see how this is working, we're going to edit our print statement at the end a bit, printing the row\_number and the dynamically created url and xpath.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# For loop, iterating over each row in our naics industry dataframe}

\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{(row\_number }\ControlFlowTok{in} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{:}\FunctionTok{nrow}\NormalTok{(naics\_industry)) \{}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Keep only the row for a given row number, get rid of every other row}
\NormalTok{    each\_row\_df }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ naics\_industry }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{slice}\NormalTok{(row\_number) }
      
    \CommentTok{\# Define url of page to get}
\NormalTok{    url }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ each\_row\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{sector\_url}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Define id of table to ingest}
\NormalTok{    xpath\_employment\_table }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{paste0}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}//*[@id="\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,each\_row\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{sector\_xpath\_id,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}"]\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
    
    \CommentTok{\# To help us see what\textquotesingle{}s happening as we build this, we\textquotesingle{}re going to print the thing we\textquotesingle{}re creating.  }
    \FunctionTok{print}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{paste0}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"ROW NUMBER:"}\NormalTok{, row\_number,}\StringTok{" URL: "}\NormalTok{,url,}\StringTok{" XPATH:"}\NormalTok{,xpath\_employment\_table))}
      
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

Armed with the URL and xpath for each sector web page, we can now go out and get the employment table for each sector.

We'll read in the html from the url we just stored; extract the table that has the xpath ID we just created; and then transform the html table code into a proper dataframe.

The dataframe is hidden inside a nested list, which we'll have to extract in the next step.

So, when you run this code, it will print out 19 dataframes inside of nested lists, each containing one dataframe.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# For loop, iterating over each row in our naics industry dataframe}

\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{(row\_number }\ControlFlowTok{in} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{:}\FunctionTok{nrow}\NormalTok{(naics\_industry)) \{}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Keep only the row for a given row number, get rid of every other row}
\NormalTok{    each\_row\_df }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ naics\_industry }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{slice}\NormalTok{(row\_number) }
      
    \CommentTok{\# Define url of page to get}
\NormalTok{    url }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ each\_row\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{sector\_url}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Define id of table to ingest}
\NormalTok{    xpath\_employment\_table }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{paste0}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}//*[@id="\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,each\_row\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{sector\_xpath\_id,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}"]\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Get employment table from each page by going to each url defined above, reading in the html with read\_html(), extracting the table with the id generated by the xpath code using html\_elements), and then turning the html into a proper dataframe using html\_table(). The dataframe is in a nested list, which we\textquotesingle{}ll have to extract in the next step.}
\NormalTok{    employment\_info }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ url }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{read\_html}\NormalTok{() }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{html\_elements}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{xpath =}\NormalTok{ xpath\_employment\_table) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{html\_table}\NormalTok{() }
    
    \CommentTok{\# To help us see what\textquotesingle{}s happening as we build this, we\textquotesingle{}re going to print the thing we\textquotesingle{}re creating.  }
    \FunctionTok{print}\NormalTok{(employment\_info)}
    
      
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

In this next step, we use employment\_info \textless- employment\_info{[}{[}1{]}{]} to extract each dataframe from the nested list. Then we'll tidy up the dataframe a bit. We'll use the get rid of all the information we don't need in the table, by using slice() to keep only the second row. We'll also standardize the column names with clean\_names().

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# For loop, iterating over each row in our naics industry dataframe}

\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{(row\_number }\ControlFlowTok{in} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{:}\FunctionTok{nrow}\NormalTok{(naics\_industry)) \{}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Keep only the row for a given row number, get rid of every other row}
\NormalTok{    each\_row\_df }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ naics\_industry }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{slice}\NormalTok{(row\_number) }
      
    \CommentTok{\# Define url of page to get}
\NormalTok{    url }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ each\_row\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{sector\_url}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Define id of table to ingest}
\NormalTok{    xpath\_employment\_table }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{paste0}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}//*[@id="\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,each\_row\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{sector\_xpath\_id,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}"]\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Get employment table from each page by going to each url defined above, reading in the html with read\_html(), extracting the table with the id generated by the xpath code using html\_elements), and then turning the html into a proper dataframe using html\_table().  The dataframe is in a nested list, which we\textquotesingle{}ll have to extract in the next step.}
\NormalTok{    employment\_info }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ url }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{read\_html}\NormalTok{() }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{html\_elements}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{xpath =}\NormalTok{ xpath\_employment\_table) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{html\_table}\NormalTok{() }
    
    \CommentTok{\# Grab the dataframe out of the list (it\textquotesingle{}s the first and only element inside the list); clean up the field names with clean\_names(); use slice(2) to keep only the second row; }
\NormalTok{    employment\_info }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ employment\_info[[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]] }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{clean\_names}\NormalTok{() }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{slice}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{) }
    
    \CommentTok{\# To help us see what\textquotesingle{}s happening as we build this, we\textquotesingle{}re going to print the thing we\textquotesingle{}re creating.  }
    \FunctionTok{print}\NormalTok{(employment\_info)}
    
      
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

##   data_series                       backdata jul_2021 aug_2021 sep_2021 oct_2021
##   <chr>                             <chr>    <chr>    <chr>    <chr>    <chr>   
## 1 Employment, all employees  (seas~ ""       5,709    5,745    (p)5,735 (p)5,768
\end{verbatim}

We now have 19 dataframes, each containing one row each and two columns, one of which is the employment number for a given sector for jul\_2021. But we're missing information about what industry sector these employment numbers represent.

We can add that back in by using bind\_cols() to reconnect the each\_row\_df, which contains the sector code and the sector name.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# For loop, iterating over each row in our naics industry dataframe}

\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{(row\_number }\ControlFlowTok{in} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{:}\FunctionTok{nrow}\NormalTok{(naics\_industry)) \{}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Keep only the row for a given row number, get rid of every other row}
\NormalTok{    each\_row\_df }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ naics\_industry }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{slice}\NormalTok{(row\_number) }
      
    \CommentTok{\# Define url of page to get}
\NormalTok{    url }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ each\_row\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{sector\_url}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Define id of table to ingest}
\NormalTok{    xpath\_employment\_table }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{paste0}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}//*[@id="\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,each\_row\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{sector\_xpath\_id,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}"]\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Get employment table from each page by going to each url defined above, reading in the html with read\_html(), extracting the table with the id generated by the xpath code using html\_elements), and then turning the html into a proper dataframe using html\_table().  The dataframe is in a nested list, which we\textquotesingle{}ll have to extract in the next step.}
\NormalTok{    employment\_info }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ url }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{read\_html}\NormalTok{() }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{html\_elements}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{xpath =}\NormalTok{ xpath\_employment\_table) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{html\_table}\NormalTok{() }
    
    \CommentTok{\# Grab the dataframe out of the list (it\textquotesingle{}s the first and only element inside the list); clean up the field names with clean\_names(); use slice(2) to keep only the second row; use bind\_cols() to append the sector code and name to this table.}
\NormalTok{    employment\_info }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ employment\_info[[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]] }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{clean\_names}\NormalTok{() }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{slice}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%} 
      \FunctionTok{bind\_cols}\NormalTok{(each\_row\_df) }
    
    \CommentTok{\# To help us see what\textquotesingle{}s happening as we build this, we\textquotesingle{}re going to print the thing we\textquotesingle{}re creating.  }
    \FunctionTok{print}\NormalTok{(employment\_info)}
    
      
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

Then we'll do a little bit of cleaning.

Let's use parse\_number() to remove the comma from the jul\_2021 number and convert it from a character to number. We'll use rename() to make the jul\_2021 column name a little more descriptive. And then we'll use select() to keep only the columns we want to keep -- the sector number, the sector name, and the jul\_2021 employment number.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# For loop, iterating over each row in our naics industry dataframe}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{(row\_number }\ControlFlowTok{in} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{:}\FunctionTok{nrow}\NormalTok{(naics\_industry)) \{}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Keep only the row for a given row number, get rid of every other row}
\NormalTok{    each\_row\_df }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ naics\_industry }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{slice}\NormalTok{(row\_number) }
      
    \CommentTok{\# Define url of page to get}
\NormalTok{    url }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ each\_row\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{sector\_url}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Define id of table to ingest}
\NormalTok{    xpath\_employment\_table }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{paste0}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}//*[@id="\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,each\_row\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{sector\_xpath\_id,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}"]\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Get employment table from each page by going to each url defined above, reading in the html with read\_html(), extracting the table with the id generated by the xpath code using html\_elements), and then turning the html into a proper dataframe using html\_table().  The dataframe is in a nested list, which we\textquotesingle{}ll have to extract in the next step.}
\NormalTok{    employment\_info }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ url }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{read\_html}\NormalTok{() }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{html\_elements}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{xpath =}\NormalTok{ xpath\_employment\_table) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{html\_table}\NormalTok{() }
    
    \CommentTok{\# Grab the dataframe out of the list (it\textquotesingle{}s the first and only element inside the list); clean up the field names with clean\_names(); use slice(2) to keep only the second row; use bind\_cols() to append the sector code and name to this table; turn jul\_2021 column into a proper number, and rename it.  Then select only three columns we need. }
\NormalTok{    employment\_info }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ employment\_info[[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]] }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{clean\_names}\NormalTok{() }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{slice}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%} 
      \FunctionTok{bind\_cols}\NormalTok{(each\_row\_df) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{jul\_2021 =} \FunctionTok{parse\_number}\NormalTok{(jul\_2021)) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{rename}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{jul\_2021\_employees =}\NormalTok{ jul\_2021) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{select}\NormalTok{(sector,description,jul\_2021\_employees) }
    
    \CommentTok{\# To help us see what\textquotesingle{}s happening as we build this, we\textquotesingle{}re going to print the thing we\textquotesingle{}re creating.  }
    \FunctionTok{print}\NormalTok{(employment\_info)}
    
    
\NormalTok{\}}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

We're getting very close to the finished table we showed at the beginning.

But right now, each bit of sector information is separated between 19 different dataframes.

We want them in one dataframe.

We can fix this by creating an empty dataframe called ``employment\_by\_sector\_all'' using tibble(), placing it before our ``for loop''.

And inside our ``for loop'' at the end, we'll bind each employment\_info dataframe to the newly created empty dataframe.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Create an empty dataframe to hold results }
\NormalTok{employment\_by\_sector\_all }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{tibble}\NormalTok{()}

\CommentTok{\# For loop, iterating over each row in our naics industry dataframe}
\ControlFlowTok{for}\NormalTok{(row\_number }\ControlFlowTok{in} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{:}\FunctionTok{nrow}\NormalTok{(naics\_industry)) \{}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Keep only the row for a given row number, get rid of every other row}
\NormalTok{    each\_row\_df }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ naics\_industry }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{slice}\NormalTok{(row\_number) }
      
    \CommentTok{\# Define url of page to get}
\NormalTok{    url }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ each\_row\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{sector\_url}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Define id of table to ingest}
\NormalTok{    xpath\_employment\_table }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{paste0}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}//*[@id="\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{,each\_row\_df}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{sector\_xpath\_id,}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}"]\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
    
    \CommentTok{\# Get employment table from each page by going to each url defined above, reading in the html with read\_html(), extracting the table with the id generated by the xpath code using html\_elements), and then turning the html into a proper dataframe using html\_table().  The dataframe is in a nested list, which we\textquotesingle{}ll have to extract in the next step.}
\NormalTok{    employment\_info }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ url }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{read\_html}\NormalTok{() }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{html\_elements}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{xpath =}\NormalTok{ xpath\_employment\_table) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{html\_table}\NormalTok{() }
    
    \CommentTok{\# Grab the dataframe out of the list (it\textquotesingle{}s the first and only element inside the list); clean up the field names with clean\_names(); use slice(2) to keep only the second row; use bind\_cols() to append the sector code and name to this table; turn jul\_2021 column into a proper number, and rename it.  Then select only three columns we need. }
\NormalTok{    employment\_info }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ employment\_info[[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]] }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{clean\_names}\NormalTok{() }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{slice}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%} 
      \FunctionTok{bind\_cols}\NormalTok{(each\_row\_df) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{jul\_2021 =} \FunctionTok{parse\_number}\NormalTok{(jul\_2021)) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{rename}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{jul\_2021\_employees =}\NormalTok{ jul\_2021) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{select}\NormalTok{(sector,description,jul\_2021\_employees) }
    
    \CommentTok{\# Bind each individual employment info table to our employment\_by\_sector\_all dataframe}
\NormalTok{    employment\_by\_sector\_all }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ employment\_by\_sector\_all }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
      \FunctionTok{bind\_rows}\NormalTok{(employment\_info)}
    
\NormalTok{\}}

\CommentTok{\# Display the completed dataframe}
\NormalTok{employment\_by\_sector\_all}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}
